t: Length of the Longest Valid Substring
o: A substring is valid if it contains no forbidden string as a substring. Key bound: forbidden strings have length ≤ 10, so whether the window [l, r] is valid depends only on the last ≤10 characters ending at r. Sweep r left to right maintaining the smallest valid left bound l; for each r, examine every substring of word ending at r with length 1..min(10, r−l+1); if any is forbidden, l must move past its start. Since l only moves forward, the total work is O(n · 10) substring hashes. Example 1: "cbaaaabc" with forbidden {aaa, cb}: when r reaches the second 'a' of "aaa", l jumps past the first 'a', ultimately allowing "aabc" of length 4.
k: Forbidden lengths ≤ 10 means validity of [l, r] is determined locally near r.
Two pointers: l only moves right; each r triggers at most 10 hash-set lookups.

a.n: Approach 1: Sliding Window with Bounded Back-Checks
a.i: Put all forbidden strings in a hash set. For each right endpoint r, check substrings word[r-L+1..r] for L = 1..10; whenever one is forbidden at start position p, set l = max(l, p+1). The window [l, r] is then guaranteed valid, and the answer is the max window size.
s: Store forbidden strings in a set.
For r from 0 to n-1, for L from 1 to min(10, r+1): if word[r-L+1..r] is forbidden, l = max(l, r-L+2).
a.t: O(n · 10 · L̄) — 10 substring extractions/hashes per position
a.sp: O(total forbidden characters) — the hash set

a.n: Approach 2: Precompute Nearest Forbidden End per Position
a.i: Alternative framing: for each r compute the latest start position of any forbidden string ending at r (call it hit[r], or −1). Then l(r) = max over windows; equivalently maintain l = max(l, hit[r]+1) — same complexity, sometimes cleaner conceptually.
s: For each r and length L ≤ 10, if the substring is forbidden record hit[r] = max(hit[r], r−L+1).
Sweep r advancing l past hit[r] and track the max window.

w: Lead with Approach 1; mention Aho–Corasick as the theoretical optimum if forbidden lengths were unbounded. Pitfall: must break the inner loop when r−L+1 < l (substring would start outside the window and moving l backwards is wrong). Follow-up: what if forbidden strings can be up to length 100? Then Aho–Corasick automaton becomes necessary.
